_about: THE PETUNIA (Petunia x atkinsiana, the garden petunia): a low sprawling mound of soft, sticky, hairy oval leaves, its stems trailing out and turning up, smothered all summer in wide trumpets -- five lobes fused into one flaring funnel, velvety purple, pink, white or red, veined darker into a dark throat. A bedding flower of the 19th century's parks and window boxes. Its LOOK, painted into the flowers' atlas (plants/flowers.js): petal / petal2 / centre / leaf / spike -- shape, colours (a list: one a variant), throat, veins and touches.
